task:
Document core.jsonc from the native C++ code, which is the single source of truth for keys, types and defaults. Config keys are registered across the C++ source (start with src/server/configuration/configuration.cpp, then grep for where keys are read/registered, e.g. src/monitor/consolelogger/consolelogger.cpp and src/server/commands/manager.cpp; grep for key names such as CommandPrefixes, Rotation, Unlocker, Menu, SteamAuth).
Cover every key you can verify in the C++ code, including nested ones.
Then compare against plugin_files/configs/core.example.jsonc on the beta branch. For every key the C++ code supports that the example lacks (or has with a wrong default/type), update the example with write_upstream_file, keeping its existing JSONC style and comments. Do not remove keys unless the C++ code no longer has them.

Use plugin_files/configs/confilter.example.jsonc (and the console filter code that loads it) to explain the console filter config file format, its rules and the `sw confilter` commands.
Note the config path in the page may be wrong; verify it in the code.

Find every command-line option the C++/native code reads, e.g.
`CommandLine()->ParmValue(CUtlStringToken("-sw_logpath"), WIN_LINUX("addons\\swiftlys2\\logs", "addons/swiftlys2/logs"))`
where the token is the CLI option and the second argument is the default value.
Also look for other CommandLine() accessors (HasParm, ParmValue, CheckParm, ...) using sw_ options.
Update the options table (option, example, details incl. default and accepted values).

Ensure the page's code examples only use members that exist in this API. Do not describe internals.
